text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- 44 percent of patients in mental care undergo forced treatment, more than in other EU countries, study shows.
- NATO Awacs surveillance plane to visit Finland in August as part of Partnership for Peace programme.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto will not join Baltic ministers' meeting in Norway due to fever but spokeswoman says illness just a flu.
- Algae situation in the Gulf of Finland to be monitored from ferries between Helsinki and Tallinn.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Expected rise in real estate prices could boost property investment companies' shares: a 20 percent rise in prices would bring over 20 percent share price gains, Merita analysts say.

- Oil and chemicals group Neste reacted to trading losses last year by salvaging what it could, and management enjoys supervisory board's confidence, says supervisory board chairman Tuulikki Hamalainen.
- Private investors have bought shares and moved into mutual funds actively this year as low interest rates make equity investment attractive, brokers say.
- Finland planning special tax for competitors to the post office to compensate for its obligation to offer services in unprofitable regions.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish political parties still wavering in their stand on EMU and only the Conservative Party clearly wants Finland to be among the first to join in the third phase.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Security police chief Seppo Nevala says extremist groups in Finland are a serious problem because their operations follow international patterns.
DEMARI

- Internal pressures in unions like the Paper Workers' Union and state unions are one of the most serious obstacle to a comprehensive pay deal next autumn, says Esa Swanljung, chairman of the Confederation of Salaried Employees.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Catamaran design could be a competitive alternative for sailing boats for families, shipbuilder says.
- Eighteen-year-old pianist Maris Gothoni's debut concert showed stunning wisdom and maturity.
